extracted.intended_audience: proofreaders, manuscript editors, authors, and production staff at publishers
extracted.subtask_short: proofreading for print and digital publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for proofreading and marking proofs for print and electronic publications, including rules for hyphenation, typography, pagination, illustrations/tables, PDF annotation tools, and responsibilities for tracked errors. Applies to authors, proofreaders, editors, and production teams preparing final publications across formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark each change throughout proofs (no global indication unless systemic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each change must be marked throughout the proofs (if possible, the PDF should be searched to find and evaluate other instances of the term).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not indicate a particular term change only once global unless it is a systemic problem; search PDFs for other instances; when systemic, consider a single 'global' instruction but be cautious about pagination/index impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread end-of-line hyphenation and word breaks
rubrics_metrics.description: End-of-line hyphenation should be checked, especially in proper names and terms outside dictionary ranges; the first proofs are usually the first time words have been divided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Merriam-Webster’s Collegiate Dictionary recommendations where applicable; for nondictionary words supply preferred hyphenation or an editor's style sheet to typesetter. Prefer a liberal approach; avoid more than three succeeding lines ending in a hyphen. For dividing URLs, follow specialized guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide nondictionary hyphenation or style sheet to typesetter
rubrics_metrics.description: For words or names not listed in a dictionary, a list of nondictionary words and their preferred hyphenation (or an editor’s style sheet) should be submitted to the typesetter with the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents inconsistent hyphenation and avoids creating tight/loose lines; helps typesetter maintain consistent breaks throughout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typeface and font consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each element in proofs (chapter numbers and titles, subheads, text, extracts, figure captions) should be presented in a consistent typeface and style according to the design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check heads/subheads for assigned typographic levels; examine set-off material for font, size, indentation; ensure italics/bold/small caps start and stop as intended. Watch for conversion errors (dropped/transmuted special characters or invisible comments). For systemic font errors, alert publisher if pagination/index will be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert publisher immediately for systemic errors that affect pagination
rubrics_metrics.description: When a systemic problem is identified—especially one for a printed work that will affect pagination across more than a few pages and therefore the index—the publisher should be alerted immediately in case new first proofs are needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Global instructions may be preferable to avoid cluttering proofs, but early communication is required if repagination will result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check page numbers and running heads
rubrics_metrics.description: Page numbers and running heads must be checked to ensure presence/absence where appropriate and that the correct page number appears following a blank page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify typesetter followed recto/verso/two-page spread instructions; running heads must be proofread for placement; for running heads to endnotes, verify or supply page numbers by checking corresponding pages of text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify illustrations' placement, orientation, size, and captions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreader must verify that all illustrations appear in the right location in the text, in the right size, right side up, not flopped or distorted, and with their own captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check locators in captions refer accurately to parts of illustrations; ensure that full-page illustrations omit running heads/page numbers unless design dictates. If several full pages of illustrations occur, consider requesting page numbers or running heads to orient readers. For two-page broadsides, ensure they fall on facing pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread tables for content and alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables must be proofread both for content and for alignment, and lists of illustrations/tables should be checked against captions and page numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure tables presented as two-page broadsides fall on facing pages; verify page numbers in lists and add if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check overall appearance: page length, spacing, running heads, and typographic defects
rubrics_metrics.description: Each page or pair of facing pages should be checked for length, vertical spacing, position of running heads and page numbers, and other conformity to design specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag fuzzy type, incomplete letters, blocks of lighter/darker type; query 'Type OK?' or 'Too dark?'. Note more than three consecutive hyphenated line-ends; ensure page doesn't end with a subhead; avoid widow (page beginning with last line of paragraph unless full measure). Last word in paragraph must not be hyphenated unless at least four letters carry over. Words may break across a spread (verso to recto) but usually not at end of a spread (recto to verso).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit successive hyphenated line-ends to three
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than three succeeding lines should end in a hyphen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If more occur, indicate adjustments; see other referenced sections for hyphenation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check facing pages for alignment and allow line-length adjustments to avoid widows
rubrics_metrics.description: Facing pages of text must align, but it is usually acceptable for both pages to run a line long or short to avoid widows or to accommodate corrections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typesetting can be adjusted (looser/tighter) to add or remove lines; typesetter may add space above a subhead so facing pages match length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofread for sense (logic, garbled, repeated, missing text) but avoid substantive rewriting
rubrics_metrics.description: The proofreader must query—or correct, if possible—illogical, garbled, repeated, or missing text; any rewriting must be limited to correction of fact or of gross syntactical error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive and stylistic changes should have been completed at editing stage; avoid changes that would alter page makeup across more than a couple pages to prevent expensive repagination and index effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to mark proofs: corrections in margin and mark in text
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections must always be written in the margin next to the line concerned and a mark placed in the text (caret for addition, line through for deletion) to indicate where a correction is to be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Never write corrections only between lines; if multiple corrections on a line, mark them in margin in order separated by vertical lines. Use guideline/arrow only when correction cannot be written next to the line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Circle verbal instructions on proofs to indicate they are instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Verbal instructions written on proofs—such as 'see attached typescript' or 'ital' or 'rom'—should be circled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circling shows these are instructions and words/abbreviations themselves should not be incorporated into the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use conventional proofreaders' marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the commonly understood proofreaders' marks that typesetters and publishing personnel understand; adapted marks form the basis of PDF annotation tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarity with marks facilitates transfer of corrections whether on paper or PDF; see figures illustrating marks for deletion, insertion, spacing, typography, punctuation, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate extensive changes clearly (rewrite in margin or use separate document)
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever marks required to fix a line or two threaten to become illegible, cross out whole passage and rewrite it correctly in the margin; if not enough room, make a separate document indicating insertion points in both places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid repagination, match word count of new material to old; for transposed material circle passage and mark new location; most global changes should nonetheless be marked individually to ensure correctness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make marks legible and distinct from publisher/type-setter marks
rubrics_metrics.description: All corrections must be written clearly in upper- and lowercase letters; red proof markings are often preferred for visibility but any distinct color will do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pen or pencil but be ready to erase unwanted marks; ensure hand-marked corrections intended for electronic transmission are dark enough to scan and not extending to page edges. Messy or indistinct marks may be overlooked or cause further errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark deletions without obliterating text; circle punctuation to be removed
rubrics_metrics.description: To remove letters/words draw diagonal/straight line through item and write delete mark in margin; punctuation to be removed should be circled rather than crossed through so it remains visible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitutions should be written in margin next to struck text. Use delete-and-close-up only when deleting a letter or hyphen within a word or when adjoining remaining material with no space. Do not obliterate original text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate spacing adjustments with standard marks
rubrics_metrics.description: When spaces within a line are unequal, insert carets and write 'eq #' in the margin; to delete space use close-up mark; to add space insert a vertical line and write space mark (#) in the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The space mark also indicates need for vertical space/leading between lines. Use consistent marks and document desired spacing changes clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark paragraphing and indent changes using standard symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an L-shaped mark in the text and paragraph mark (¶) in margin to indicate a new paragraph; to run paragraphs together draw a line and write 'run in'; use squares/rectangles to indicate indents of one or more ems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat indents for consecutive lines by drawing a line from the square to the baseline of the last affected line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark position and alignment adjustments explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: If text appears too far left or right use move-right or move-left marks; use move-up/move-down for vertical adjustments; use both marks to indicate centering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert marks in text and margin; write 'fl' (flush left) or 'fr' (flush right) circled in margin for flush alignment; use vertical (||) or horizontal (=) alignment marks for tabular matter and extend marks to encompass multiple lines as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark transpositions precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: To move letters, words, or phrases circumscribe them precisely (including punctuation) and write circled 'tr' in the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For larger transpositions draw brackets around each item and include a circled instruction in the margin; clearly indicate new location and mark both original and new spots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark items to be spelled out
rubrics_metrics.description: When an abbreviation or numeral is to be spelled out, circle the item and write circled 'sp' in the margin; if ambiguous, write the full word in the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clarity to prevent mistaken expansions or formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use 'stet' to revert deletions or corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: To undelete or restore material earlier marked for deletion or correction, place a row of dots under the material, cross out the marginal mark or correction, and write 'stet' or 'stet as set' in the margin, circled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'stet' to ensure the original remains when there might be uncertainty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark capitalization and font changes with conventional marks
rubrics_metrics.description: To lowercase a capital draw a slash and write 'lc'; to capitalize draw three lines under and write 'cap'; small caps use two lines + 'sc'; italics one line + 'ital'; roman: circle + 'rom'; bold: wavy underline + 'bf'; remove bold by circling + 'not bf'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circle all marginal instructions to prevent incorporation of the instruction text; see figures for mark examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify punctuation changes and correct accents explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: To change punctuation, circle it and write the correct mark in the margin; to add punctuation insert a caret and write the mark in the margin. If an accent/diacritical is incorrect, cross out the entire letter and write the correct letter with accent in the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify punctuation clarifications (comma caret over, apostrophe inverted caret under, period circled, semicolon/colon followed by short vertical line, question/exclamation accompanied by circled 'set'). Name unusual accents (e.g., 'breve') in the margin and circle them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt conventional marks to PDF proofreading tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreading symbols and related markup for paper have been adapted for PDF readers; PDF tools include strikeout, insert/replace, highlighting, notes, and drawing shapes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF advantages: searchable text, typed annotations, automatic time/user stamps, no shipping, quick turnaround. Avoid redundant markup; choose a single tool and optionally add a virtual note stating intent. Use the annotation list to ensure items aren't missed; those making changes can mark list items as corrected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-check proofs with a checklist tailored to the work
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to routine checks, proofreader must: check article/chapter titles against TOC, verify footnote placement relative to superscript, complete cross-references, and for books verify title/half-title/copyright info; for journals check covers, spine, front/back matter, volume/issue/dates, inclusive page numbers, and copyright lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Checklist items vary by work type; for electronic formats see additional guidance. Query or delete TOC items not present in work; ensure footnotes begin on page with their reference number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign responsibility for errors using standard abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofreader may be asked to distinguish between typesetting errors and changes introduced at other stages; use abbreviations determined by the publisher such as PE (printer's error), AA (author's alteration), EA (editor's alteration), DA (designer's alteration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circle such indications so they are not incorporated into corrected proofs; use publisher's conventions for billing and responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate author's alterations (AAs) from editor's alterations (EAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A publisher's contract may permit author alterations within an AA allowance; rewriting or adding new material by the author is an AA. Corrections of errors introduced by publisher after author's review are EAs and not chargeable to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AA allowances (e.g., 5%) do not mean 5% of proofs can be altered without cost; author may be charged beyond allowance. Corrections of errors uncaught in editing are AA if the author approved the edited manuscript; supplying page numbers in lists and running heads to notes is typically an EA. For articles consult the journal publisher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist for proofing and testing electronic formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Every component of a publication must be checked and tested in its final electronic format (PDF, e-book, web, app) before publication; full text offered in more than one format must be proofread word for word in at least one format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check layout to ensure no elements missing or unintended markup; confirm special characters correctly converted (Unicode); verify internal/external links and interactive features; confirm illustrations/tables are present and functional; ensure content matches across formats or that intended variations are noted; test for valid EPUB/HTML markup; proofread recent changes in each format.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPUB QA checklist essentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific EPUB checks: scroll/page entire book on at least one reading system to look for missing content; verify metadata includes title and ISBN and matches front matter; check cover, table of contents, and start page locations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check small caps appearance on each reading system; check block quotations, lists, stanza breaks, and formatting across reading systems; be mindful of accessibility and semantic markup using correct HTML/CSS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notes, bibliography, and index checks for electronic formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Notes should be linked in both directions; footnotes in reflowable formats are usually converted to endnotes or placed after paragraph/section. Bibliographies should be properly formatted; indexes from print should be retained and links created to anchors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure 'ibid.' doesn't appear out of context (consider replacing with short forms); left-justify long URLs to avoid gaps; index entries should link directly to referenced elements; 'see'/'see also' references must link to targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image quality and format requirements for electronic publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Check all images for quality and readability on target reading systems; image resolution and file size should conform to retailer specs; images should be saved in RGB, not CMYK; use transparent backgrounds as applicable; captions should align and appear on same page as image when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CSS to scale images as necessary; test images on representative devices to ensure legibility; ensure captions link to images in index/anchors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables and charts in electronic formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Tables should be coded in HTML where possible rather than presented as images; ensure tables are legible and content fits on screen; convert simple lists to paragraph text when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check charts/graphs for legibility; charts using color should include explanations for grayscale/monochrome viewing; test table behavior in reflowable formats and on multiple devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio and video content checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Check retailer specs for multimedia content and encode/size appropriately; include proper fallbacks and poster images for videos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide fallback content or explanations when media not supported; include links to online access points for multimedia; videos should include a poster image and proper metadata per platform specs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for testing electronic formats and regression testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishers should have procedures to test each new book/article in each format in publication context using a range of devices/apps; websites and apps require earlier-stage testing and possibly beta testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform regression testing to safeguard against errors introduced by other fixes or new features; test-case documents and use-case scenarios aid systematic testing; testing timing differs for static publications vs dynamic web/apps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for electronic testing (feature/use-case/wireframe/test-case)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use feature definition documents, use-case documents, wireframes/design mockups, UI specifications, and test-case documents to describe intended functionality, behavior, and navigation for testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature definitions should specify functional details (e.g., search ordering and handling of diacritics); use-case docs describe step-by-step expected behavior; test-case docs provide actionable test instructions tied to features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate and track changes across different formats with clear location references
rubrics_metrics.description: Use augmented PDFs or content proofs that reproduce print alongside elements only in electronic formats; error reports should make the location of each reported error clear using searchable phrases or page-number references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralized databases can facilitate reports from multiple reviewers and long periods; entries combined with testing documentation can serve as a contract between editors and production to ensure each change is implemented properly.
